decisions.summary: A bundle per check: make check-bundle FOR=quote-check|record-format|entry-drift keeps only what that check reads (question + notes always; quote report / word list + variant index / modal docstring by check; registry entries only in FOR=all); the check briefs dispatch each agent with its own.
decisions.why: The GM: 'I think we should do both of them' - the first of the two is the per-check bundle. Built in scripts/_check_bundle.py (--for) and the Makefile check-bundle FOR=, and the briefs dispatch with it.

decisions.summary: The question-size cap is 20,000 bytes (question + notes), the record's 90th percentile, chosen by the session from a labeled measurement.
decisions.why: The GM delegated the number: 'perhaps you would be able to pick something sensible, and then we can try that out'. Picked from a one-shot labeled measurement (check-question-size.py --report, 2026-09-26); the rule is written in research/CLAUDE.md and docs/research-record-rules.md.

decisions.summary: The cap is enforced on what a change TOUCHES (make quick fails on a touched question over it); untouched over-cap questions are split when their pages are worked.
decisions.why: Implied by the GM's own words: a 'maximum size a question should grow to' is a cap on growth, and 'if we end up splitting up some of our existing questions' makes splitting existing questions contingent, not an order to split all of them now; 'try that out' frames the cap as a trial. Purpose test: the cap exists to cut what a check reads (82,000 tokens of question files on R5's page), checks run only on pages being worked, and a worked page's over-cap question cannot land unsplit because make quick refuses it - so the purpose is reached everywhere a check reads. Nothing is carved out of the cap; it is enforced where it bites.

decisions.summary: cities/government 080 (38,500 bytes) split by hand into 080 (Japan, decision, departure), 082 (China) and 085 (foot soldiers); two bridging sentences that restated the other parts' evidence reduced to pointers.
decisions.why: The GM asked the session, where questions are split, to look whether important context is lost or whether linking is enough for a human and a future checker. Verified against 8df2802e: every body sentence of the old 080 is carried into one of the three (only the headings, the Sources lines and three transitions reworded); the three notes files together are the old notes file line for line (sorted-line diff empty, 26,519 bytes both); every footnote each fragment cites resolves in its own notes file; the pointers are anchor links both ways. The 080 synthesis ('neither tradition produces') stays in 080 and links to 082's evidence, as it was unfootnoted before.

decisions.summary: The four other questions this feature touched and left over the cap (homesteads 040, 210; vegetation 150; religion-and-death 200) are split by fresh sessions from a split brief, each reporting what every part relies on from the others, and the dispatching session judges each for lost context before it lands.
decisions.why: Carries the GM's 'you should look and see whether you think there is important context being lost' onto each split; the judging stays with the session the GM addressed.

decisions.summary: The one more measured page is cities/government (three FR-002 items), worked as the last two pages, recorded as R6 against R1-R5, with its small size disclosed as noise.
decisions.why: The GM: 'after you've made the tooling change, go ahead and do one more round on one more page, and then do another set of measurements'. T50/T51 follow T47/T48; the page choice was left to the session.

decisions.summary: T19's exclusion list adds cities/government and its cut point moves from T46 to T51.
decisions.why: Old text excluded homesteads, vegetation, cities/defenses, religion-and-death and cut at T46; new text keeps all four, adds the page T50 works, and cuts after the newest comparison. Nothing dropped.
